definitions.explanation: Attached to the stem of a verb to indicate continued action.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{勉強|べんきょう}し{続|つづ}けている。
{雨|あめ}が{三日|みっか}も{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: It has been raining for three days straight.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{何|なに}も{言|い}わずに{歩|ある}き{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: He kept walking without saying anything.

examples.japanese: {諦|あきら}めずに{努力|どりょく}し{続|つづ}ければ、いつか{夢|ゆめ}がかなうと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think that if you keep trying without giving up, your dream will come true someday.

notes:
～{続|つづ}ける is an auxiliary verb meaning "to continue doing."

PATTERN:
Verb stem + {続|つづ}ける

EXAMPLES:
- {読|よ}み{続|つづ}ける: to continue reading
- {待|ま}ち{続|つづ}ける: to keep waiting
- {走|はし}り{続|つづ}ける: to keep running
- {働|はたら}き{続|つづ}ける: to keep working
- {歩|ある}き{続|つづ}ける: to keep walking

NUANCE:
～{続|つづ}ける emphasizes sustained, persistent action over time. Often implies effort or determination.

CONTRAST:
- ～{続|つづ}ける: continued action (emphasizes persistence)
- ～ている: ongoing state (simple progressive)
